Interface SortedMultiset<E>

Type Parameters:
E - the element type
All Superinterfaces:
Collection<E>, Iterable<E>, Multiset<E>, SequencedCollection<E>
All Known Implementing Classes:
TreeMultiset
public interface SortedMultiset<E> extends Multiset<E>, SequencedCollection<E>
A multiset that keeps its elements sorted, by their natural ordering or by a comparator: the multiset counterpart of NavigableSet. It iterates over its elements in ascending order, each as many times as it occurs. Its entry set, element set and the views it returns follow the same order.

As a SequencedCollection, its first and last elements are the lowest and the highest: SequencedCollection.getFirst() returns the lowest element, and SequencedCollection.removeFirst() removes one occurrence of it. SequencedCollection.addFirst(Object) and SequencedCollection.addLast(Object) throw UnsupportedOperationException, since the order decides where an element goes.

The views of a range of a sorted multiset, and its reversed view, are live: changes to the view show in the multiset, and the other way around. A range view rejects elements outside its range with IllegalArgumentException.

Since:
0.1.1
